beginner.headline: TV Star Tommy Walsh Dies at 69
beginner.brief: TV star Tommy Walsh died at the age of 69. He worked as a builder before he became famous on TV. He got his chance on TV after he fixed up a house for someone at the BBC. He was on the BBC show Ground Force from 1997 to 2005. The team gave people’s gardens a new look. He joined the TV show Homes Under the Hammer in 2021. His agent said Walsh died peacefully after a long illness, with his family around him.

intermediate.headline: TV presenter Tommy Walsh dies at 69
intermediate.brief: Tommy Walsh, a building and DIY expert who starred on several television shows, has died at the age of 69. His agent told BBC News that Walsh died peacefully after a long illness, with his family around him, and asked for privacy for the family. Walsh worked as a professional builder before becoming known to television audiences. He got his big break after restoring the home of a BBC producer who was developing ideas for a show that later became Ground Force. Walsh said he turned down the offer to appear on the show three times. He said he agreed after his eight-year-old daughter told him about a £10 bet she had made with a boy at school. She had bet that her father would appear on television. Walsh appeared on the BBC’s Ground Force with Alan Titchmarsh and Charlie Dimmock from 1997 to 2005. On Ground Force, Walsh’s co-stars carried out makeovers on gardens that belonged to members of the public. He went on to present Cowboys and Angels as well as Clean It, Fix It. In 2021, Walsh joined the daytime programme Homes Under the Hammer. Walsh also published several books about DIY projects that people can do themselves.

advanced.headline: Ground Force Star Tommy Walsh Dies at 69
advanced.brief: Tommy Walsh, known for his work on Ground Force, Homes Under the Hammer and Challenge Tommy Walsh, has died aged 69. Walsh was a builder by trade before rising to prominence alongside Alan Titchmarsh and Charlie Dimmock on the BBC’s Ground Force, where he appeared from 1997 to 2005. Walsh’s television breakthrough came after he renovated the home of a BBC producer who was developing ideas for what would become Ground Force. Walsh told the BBC in 2004 that the producer had asked him to look at two pilots, or trial episodes, one of which was a forerunner to Ground Force called Over the Garden Wall. He gave a blunt assessment of that pilot, likening the experience to watching paint dry. Walsh said he declined the offer to appear on Ground Force three times. He said he relented when his eight-year-old daughter told him she had wagered £10 with a boy at school that her father would appear on television. Walsh and his co-stars found a winning formula in transforming gardens for members of the public. Walsh later fronted Cowboys and Angels as well as Clean It, Fix It. In 2021, he began appearing on Homes Under the Hammer, a popular daytime programme. His work extended beyond broadcasting, with several do-it-yourself books to his name. Earlier reports said he had undergone surgery for throat cancer in 2022 and for lung cancer in 2023. His agent told BBC News that Walsh had died peacefully after a prolonged illness, with his family around him, and asked for the family to be given privacy.
